draft.title: The Civil War and 1949
card: The Nationalists and Communists resumed their civil war after Japan surrendered in 1945. The Nationalist government, led by Jiang Jieshi, had the larger army and more weapons, and held the major cities.
The Nationalists lost support. Prices rose very fast, officials were often corrupt, and many people lost faith in the government.
The Communist People's Liberation Army won over many peasants, gained captured weapons and soldiers, and took Manchuria in 1948. It then won major battles and took Beijing in early 1949.
On 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China in Beijing. Jiang Jieshi and the Nationalists withdrew to the island of Taiwan.
draft.remember: The Communists won because Nationalist support collapsed while their own grew, and they proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949.

a.q: Why were the Nationalists defeated in the civil war, even though they began with a larger army?
opts: They lost public support while the Communists gained it
They ran out of weapons before the war began
Their army was defeated in Taiwan before 1945
Japan joined the Communists against them in 1948
a.why: The Nationalists began with more soldiers and weapons, but rising prices and corruption cost them support. The Communists gained peasant support and captured weapons. A larger army did not guarantee victory, so the first wrong option is tempting but ignores this.
a.clue: Think about who the people trusted by 1949.

b.q: In 1949 Mao Zedong stood in Beijing and proclaimed a new state. Which statement best describes what happened to the Nationalists?
opts: Their leaders withdrew to Taiwan after losing the mainland
Their leaders joined the new government in Beijing
Their leaders surrendered to Japan and left China
Their leaders stayed on the mainland and ruled the south
b.why: After defeat on the mainland, Jiang Jieshi and the Nationalists withdrew to Taiwan. The People's Republic was proclaimed on the mainland, so the Nationalists did not keep control of the south or share power in Beijing.
b.clue: Where did Jiang Jieshi go after losing the mainland?

a.best: They lost public support while the Communists gained it

b.best: Their leaders withdrew to Taiwan after losing the mainland

problems.detail: The clue 'Where did Jiang Jieshi go after losing the mainland?' repeats the right option's exact phrase 'after losing the mainland', so a student can match it without knowing the idea.
The right option is the longest and the only one with an extra precise detail ('after losing the mainland'), so it stands out from the distractors.
The why says 'the first wrong option is tempting', but options are shown in random order, and no wrong option is about the larger army. The reference is confusing and does not match any distractor.

The distractors (Japan joining the Communists in 1948, the army being defeated in Taiwan before 1945) are implausible, and the clue points straight to the answer. This is too easy for Year 12 VCE Revolutions.

proposal.title: The civil war and 1949
card: The Nationalists and Communists resumed their civil war after Japan surrendered in 1945. The Nationalist government, led by Jiang Jieshi, had the larger army, more weapons and aid from the United States, and held the major cities.
The Nationalists lost support. Prices rose very fast, officials were often corrupt, and many people lost faith in the government.
The Communist People's Liberation Army won over many peasants, gained captured weapons and soldiers, and took Manchuria in 1948. It then won major battles and took Beijing in early 1949.
On 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the People's Republic of China in Beijing. Jiang Jieshi and the Nationalists withdrew to the island of Taiwan.
proposal.remember: The Communists won because Nationalist support collapsed while their own grew, and they proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949.

a.q: Why were the Nationalists defeated in the civil war, even though they began with a larger army?
opts: They lost public support while the Communists gained it
The Communists had more foreign aid and weapons from 1945
The Communists held most major cities from the start
Peasants backed them, but city workers turned against them
a.why: Rising prices and corruption cost the Nationalists support, while the Communists won over peasants and captured weapons. It was the Nationalists, not the Communists, who began with more weapons, US aid and the major cities.
a.clue: Think beyond the size of each army.

b.q: Which statement best describes China at the end of 1949?
opts: Communists ruled the mainland, Nationalists held Taiwan
Nationalists ruled the mainland, Communists held Taiwan
Communists and Nationalists shared a government in Beijing
Communists ruled the north, Nationalists held the south
b.why: Mao proclaimed the People's Republic in Beijing after the Communists won the mainland, and Jiang Jieshi's Nationalists withdrew to Taiwan. A north and south split is tempting, but the Nationalists did not keep a part of the mainland.
b.clue: Which side proclaimed a new state, and where did the other side go?

a.best: They lost public support while the Communists gained it

b.best: Communists ruled the mainland, Nationalists held Taiwan
